verdict.rationale: Vercel's own access-token docs say every token carries a scope at personal, team, or project level. A project-scoped token denies requests outside its project, which keeps jobs, tools, and workflows confined to the projects they need: least-privilege credentials an agent can use. Missing for 10: operation-level permission scopes (e.g. read-only versus deploy), token expiry or rotation controls, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Every token carries a scope that determines which resources it can reach

A project-scoped token denies any request to another project, to a user-level resource, or to a team-level resource. This keeps jobs, tools, and workflows constrained to the projects they need rather than granting them the entire team or your full account.
Vercel access tokens authenticate requests to the Vercel REST API and the Vercel CLI on your behalf.
